title: Limits of Satan’s Power
definition: The doctrine of Limits of Satan’s Power teaches that satan is real and dangerous, but he is limited, created, judged, and unable to overthrow God’s sovereign rule.
summary: Limits of Satan’s Power names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Satan is real and dangerous, but he is limited, created, judged, and unable to overthrow God’s sovereign rule. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Limits of Satan’s Power because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Satan is real and dangerous, but he is limited, created, judged, and unable to overthrow God’s sovereign rule. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people either give Satan too much credit or too little attention when they do not see his limits under God. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not speak of Satan as though he is everywhere or all-powerful. Fear God, resist evil, and rest in the Lord’s authority. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
